newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Western Digital opens second Malaysian plant.
newsitem.headline: Western Digital opens second Malaysian plant.

text.p: Disk drive maker Western Digital Corp on Thursday opened its second Malaysian plant, a 200 million ringgit ($80 million) facility to make desktop PC disk drives.

The 270,000 sq ft Malaysia plant follows the launch of another facility on Wednesday in Singapore to make high-end hard disk enterprise drives designed for workstations and local area network (LAN) servers.
In a statement, Irvine, California-based Western Digital said its Malaysian plants were expected to produce over 50,000 drives per day by 1997.
The new plant will produce various capacity points of Western Digital's Caviar line of disk drives, which range in capacity from 850 megabytes to 3.1 gigabytes.

The Caviar drives account for 16 percent of the international market, the company said. The disk drive industry produces over 100 million units of product a year, bringing in revenues of nearly $30 billion.

The expansion of hard drive manufacturing for Western Digital's Personal Storage group in Malaysia was expected to provide the firm with sufficient manufacturing capacity through the decade, the statement said.
The first Western Digital factory in Malaysia, opened 23 years ago, cost 70 million ringgit.
Of the 15 million disk drives made by the company last year, about a third were made in Malaysia.

Western Digital president Charles Haggerty told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday that the company planned to spend $100 million to double the disk drive output of its plants in Singapore and Malaysia.
Analysts estimate the disk drive industry's growth will continue at a 20 percent-plus annual rate through the end of the decade.
Eighty percent of the world's disk drives are made by just four companies, including Western Digital.
In fiscal 1996 ended June 29, Western Digital reported net income of $96.9 million, or $2.01 per share, versus $123.3 million, or $2.47 per share.
Revenue for the year totalled a record $2.87 billion versus $2.13 billion.
